meadow.name: Badger Setts
meadow.blurb: Tunnels under the meadow, worn smooth by generations of badgers.
meadow.clue: Grandpa used to speak of badger setts under the meadow, so deep the badgers came up smelling of wet stone.
meadow.payoff: The setts go down and down, and they smell of wet stone. Grandpa was right.

meadow.name: The Old Well
meadow.blurb: A dry well shaft the badgers broke into, lined with mossy brick.
meadow.clue: Grandpa used to speak of an old well in the meadow, filled in before he was born. He said the badgers knew where it was.
meadow.payoff: Mossy brick, and a well shaft running down. The badgers knew where it was all along.

meadow.name: The Spring Below
meadow.blurb: Where the well's water went: a cold spring in a chamber of white stone.
meadow.clue: Grandpa swore the old well never ran dry. The water just went somewhere deeper, he said, and took the wishes with it.
meadow.payoff: A cold spring under the meadow, glinting with old coins and older wishes. The well never ran dry.

mixedwoods.name: Root Hollows
mixedwoods.blurb: Hollows among the roots of the great oaks, roomy enough to crawl through.
mixedwoods.clue: Grandma used to speak of hollows under the big oaks, where she hid as a girl and found things she never told anyone about.
mixedwoods.payoff: The root hollows, just as Grandma described them. No wonder she kept them to herself.

mixedwoods.name: The Root Cellar
mixedwoods.blurb: Someone shored up a hollow with planks long ago: a forgotten root cellar.
mixedwoods.clue: Grandma said someone once kept a cellar in the woods, under the roots, and never came back for what was in it.
mixedwoods.payoff: Planks and shelves under the roots: a cellar nobody came back for.

mixedwoods.name: The Taproot Hall
mixedwoods.blurb: A long hall where a single ancient taproot runs down into the dark.
mixedwoods.clue: Grandma always said the oldest oak in the woods had a root that reached the bottom of the world.
mixedwoods.payoff: One root, thick as a cart, running down into the dark. Grandma wasn't exaggerating.

oldgrowth.name: Mossy Cave
oldgrowth.blurb: A cave mouth behind a curtain of moss, cold and dripping.
oldgrowth.clue: Great-uncle Tobias used to speak of a cave behind the moss in the old-growth, where he went to cool off in summer.
oldgrowth.payoff: A cave behind the moss, cool as Great-uncle Tobias promised.

oldgrowth.name: The Dripping Gallery
oldgrowth.blurb: A long gallery where water ticks from the ceiling like a slow clock.
oldgrowth.clue: Great-uncle Tobias said the cave went on and on, and that you could tell the time down there by the dripping.
oldgrowth.payoff: Drip, drip, drip, steady as a clock. Great-uncle Tobias wasn't spinning yarns.

oldgrowth.name: The Glowing Grotto
oldgrowth.blurb: A grotto lit only by the mushrooms on its walls.
oldgrowth.clue: Great-uncle Tobias swore that deep in the cave the mushrooms gave off their own light. Nobody believed him.
oldgrowth.payoff: The walls glow green and the mushrooms light the way. Great-uncle Tobias was telling the truth.

burnscar.name: The Kiln Mouth
burnscar.blurb: The scorched mouth of an old charcoal kiln, half buried by last year's fire.
burnscar.clue: Great-grandpa used to speak of a charcoal kiln on the ridge, back when the family burned wood for a living.
burnscar.payoff: The fire cleared the ridge, and there it is: the mouth of Great-grandpa's kiln.

burnscar.name: The Collapsed Kiln
burnscar.blurb: The kiln's dome fell in long ago; you pick through its blackened ribs.
burnscar.clue: Great-grandpa said the kiln caved in one wet spring, with his tools still inside.
burnscar.payoff: Fallen brick and blackened ribs: Great-grandpa's kiln, caved in with everything in it.

burnscar.name: The Ash Vault
burnscar.blurb: Beneath the kiln, a brick vault where the charcoal was stored dry.
burnscar.clue: Great-grandpa said there was a vault under the kiln, and that it was the driest place in the valley.
burnscar.payoff: A dry brick vault beneath the ash: the driest place in the valley, as promised.

riverbank.name: The Undercut Bank
riverbank.blurb: Where the creek has carved under the willow roots: a low, damp hollow.
riverbank.clue: Great-aunt Rue used to speak of hiding places under the creek bank, where the water had eaten the earth away.
riverbank.payoff: Under the willow roots, a hollow the creek carved out: Great-aunt Rue's hiding place.

riverbank.name: The Flooded Grotto
riverbank.blurb: A grotto half full of still green water, reached by wading.
riverbank.clue: Great-aunt Rue said that when the creek ran low you could wade into a grotto where the water stood still and green.
riverbank.payoff: Still green water in a stone grotto. Great-aunt Rue waded here once, too.

riverbank.name: The Sunken Mill
riverbank.blurb: The stone footings of a mill the river swallowed long ago.
riverbank.clue: Great-aunt Rue swore there was a mill under the river once, and that on quiet nights you could hear its wheel.
riverbank.payoff: Millstones under the water, and a wheel that hasn't turned in a century. Great-aunt Rue heard right.

hollow.name: Fallen Walls
hollow.blurb: Moss-covered walls in the Hollow, too square to be stone the forest made.
hollow.clue: Grandpa used to speak of an old ruin in the forest, past the old-growth, where the walls were too straight to be natural.
hollow.payoff: Straight walls under the moss. Grandpa's old ruin in the forest, found at last.

hollow.name: The Ruined Cellar
hollow.blurb: Steps down through the ruin into a cellar choked with roots.
hollow.clue: Grandpa said the ruin had a cellar, and that his own grandfather wouldn't go down the steps.
hollow.payoff: Stone steps into a cellar full of roots. Whatever scared the old folks, it's quiet now.

hollow.name: The Old Hearth
hollow.blurb: The heart of the ruin: a great stone hearth with a mark carved over it.
hollow.clue: Grandpa had a story that the family didn't start out on the homestead at all, but somewhere deep in the Hollow.
hollow.payoff: Carved over the hearth is the family's own mark. This ruin was the first homestead.
